title: Samson Cree Nation identifies 15-year-old boy killed by RCMP
subtitle: The statement called for the officers involved to resign and for mental health support services to be increased in the community of Maskwacis
article: The Samson Cree Nation youth shot dead by police last week has been identified as Hoss Lightning, 15.
On Tuesday, Samson Coun. Izaiah Swampy-Omeasoo issued a statement on the teen's death.

The statement, which Swampy-Omeasoo said was issued with the permission of Lightning's family, called for the officers involved to resign and for mental health support services to be increased in the community of Maskwacis.
He described Lightning as a kid who called police for help in a moment of fear, only to be killed as a result.

Swampy-Omeasoo called for a "transparent and accountable" investigation, and for Treaty 6 chiefs to advocate for "greater co-operation and serious policy reforms on policing," including de-escalation training for officers "when it comes to Indigenous peoples."

A candlelight vigil was in the works with Lightning's family, Swampy-Omeasoo said, adding, "The family respectfully ask for those that wish to hold a vigil/protest/rally to please kindly approach the matriarchs of the family first."
Lightning was shot to death by two RCMP officers after calling 911 early last Friday morning.

According to an RCMP news release, Wetaskiwin RCMP received a 911 call from Lightning, who said he was being followed by people who were trying to kill him. Police caught up to him at 1:22 a.m. near 56 Street and 37A Avenue, on the south side of the central Alberta city.

"It was found that this individual was in possession of several weapons, which officers were able to confiscate," the release stated without specifying the alleged weapons. "However, a confrontation occurred, which resulted in two officers discharging their service firearms and the individual being struck."
RCMP officers "immediately" began emergency first aid and called emergency medical services, but Lightning died in hospital.
"Events like these are traumatic for everyone involved," RCMP said. "The Alberta RCMP wish to extend their profound condolences to the family, loved ones and friends of this young man.
The killing is being probed by the Alberta Serious Incident Response Team (ASIRT), which has the power to lay criminal charges against officers in consultation with the Crown.
